chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the embalming (hanut) for the deceased. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Place it in his prayer places (prostration spots).'

key_terms.الْحَنُوطِ: Embalming mixture of musk, camphor, and spices
key_terms.مَسَاجِدِهِ: His prayer places (prostration points: forehead, hands, knees, toes)

ai.seo_question: Where should embalming fragrance be applied on the deceased according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific application of 'hanut' (frankincense and musk mixture) by directing it to the 'masajid' (places of prostration) of the deceased, namely the forehead, hands, knees, and toes. This ruling emphasizes the continuity of the deceased's spiritual state, as these are the very points that touched the earth during their earthly prayers, thereby honoring their devotion. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking physical preparation of the body with its spiritual legacy.
